faq.a: Nurgul is associated with the Arabic form نُورْغُول, whose core sense is nurgul; light rose (turkish).

faq.q: What is the origin of Nurgul?
faq.a: Nurgul is associated with Arabic. Nurgul is a Turkish compound of Arabic نُور (nūr, 'light') + gül ('rose').
Yes — the underlying form نُورْغُول is Arabic.
Nurgul can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Nurgul should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Nūr occurs in the Quran as a term for light.

faq.q: What does Nurgul mean in Urdu?

faq.q: What does Nurgul mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Nurgul is rendered نورگل and carries the sense نورگل، گل نور.
A romanized syllable approximation is nur-gul. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Nurgul?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Nurgul, nurgul. Script forms are نور گل, نورګل, نورگل, نُورْغُول, नूरगुल.

faq.q: Is Nurgul a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
